newsitem.title: UK: Prudential seeks control of St James Place.
newsitem.headline: Prudential seeks control of St James Place.

text.p: British insurance giant Prudential Corporation said on Wednesday that it had offered 130 pence per share to buy up to 7.7 percent of financial services firm St James Place Capital Plc.

The bid, which is for 30.5 million shares, would raise Prudential's stake in St James to 29.9 percent. The offer pushed St James's share price up by six pence to 131-1/2p in volume of over seven million shares.
Prudential would have to pay a total consideration of 39.6 million pounds ($64.4 million) for the 7.7 percent stake. The tender offers will be made on April 28.
St James said the bid would give Prudential control of St James, which in turn already controls 51 percent of J. Rothschild Assurance.

St James said it had agreed with J.Rothschild to acquire the latter's remaining capital by offering 1.75 new St James shares for each J. Rothschild share held and issue 43.3 million new shares to buy 32.1 million J. Rothschild convertible preference shares.
St James reported a pretax profit of 33.2 million pounds in nine months to December 31, 1996. ($ = 0.615 British Pounds)
